activity.evidence: Completed certification checklist, your 90-day plan, and a screenshot of your weekly review reminder.

quiz.q: When should you add colours and final fonts to your design?
options: After the structure has been tested with users
quiz.explain: Visual design comes after the flow and layout are tested, because structural changes are cheapest early.

quiz.q: Ifeoma designs a button once in Figma and wants every copy to update when she changes it. What should she use?
quiz.explain: Figma components create a main version; every instance updates when the main component changes.

quiz.q: Which item is most important to include in a UX case study for an employer?
options: Your process, research insights, iterations and results
A list of every app you have used
quiz.explain: Employers want to see how you think: the problem, research, decisions, iterations and evidence of results.

quiz.q: Your project was tested with 5 participants and never launched. How should you describe it?
quiz.explain: Honest framing builds trust. State that it was a concept project and how many people tested it.

quiz.q: A salon owner reads your case study. What should you lead with?
options: The customer problem fixed and before-and-after results like booking time
quiz.explain: Business owners care about customers, time and complaints, so lead with the problem solved and measurable results.

quiz.q: Someone offers you a 'guaranteed UX job' if you pay a registration fee first. What should you do?
options: Pay quickly before the slot fills
Treat it as a likely scam and do not pay
Send your BVN to secure it
quiz.explain: Genuine jobs and clients do not require you to pay upfront for guaranteed work. Protect your money and personal data.

finalQuiz.q: Usability has five quality components. Which list is correct?
options: Contrast, labels, captions, alt text, targets
finalQuiz.explain: Nielsen's five components of usability are learnability, efficiency, memorability, errors and satisfaction.

finalQuiz.q: Which order matches the design thinking stages?
finalQuiz.explain: Design thinking runs empathise, define, ideate, prototype and test, repeating as needed.

finalQuiz.q: Before interviewing a trader and recording the call, what must Hadiza do first?
options: Ask for her BVN to confirm identity
Explain the purpose, time and recording, and get clear consent
Promise the app will be built
Start recording immediately to save time
finalQuiz.explain: Informed consent comes before any recording: purpose, time, recording use and the right to stop.

finalQuiz.q: Which persona detail is most acceptable?
options: A favourite colour invented to make her interesting
A goal and frustration taken from interview themes
finalQuiz.explain: Personas must be built from research findings, not invention or stereotypes.

finalQuiz.q: A card sort shows most users group 'Download certificate' with 'My courses'. Where should it go in the menu?
options: Under Settings, where the team put it
Under 'My courses' or close to it
finalQuiz.explain: Information architecture should follow users' mental models revealed by the card sort.

finalQuiz.q: Why should a user flow include error paths?
options: To make the diagram look complex
Because real users meet failed payments, taken slots and network drops, and the design must handle them
Error paths are only for developers
finalQuiz.explain: Designing what happens when things go wrong prevents users from getting stuck or losing their progress.

finalQuiz.q: In Figma, which key opens the Frame tool so you can choose a phone-sized screen?
finalQuiz.explain: F (or A) selects the Frame tool, where you can pick a phone preset.

finalQuiz.q: An error message says only 'Invalid input!'. Which heuristic does a better message such as 'Phone number should have 11 digits' support?
options: Help users recognise, diagnose, and recover from errors
finalQuiz.explain: Good error messages explain the problem in plain language and tell users how to fix it.

finalQuiz.q: A form shows errors only with a red border. Which accessibility problem is this?
finalQuiz.explain: WCAG 1.4.1 says colour must not be the only way information is shown; add text or an icon.

finalQuiz.q: Nielsen found that testing with about 5 users reveals what share of usability problems in qualitative testing?
finalQuiz.explain: His analysis showed about 85 percent of problems with 5 users, which is why he recommends small repeated rounds.

finalQuiz.q: Of 5 participants, 4 finished a task without help. What is the task success rate?
finalQuiz.explain: 4 divided by 5 equals 0.8, which is 80 percent.

finalQuiz.q: Which is the most honest line for a portfolio case study?
options: 'This app changed the lives of all users'
'Concept project; task success rose from 3 of 5 to 5 of 5 participants after two rounds of testing'
finalQuiz.explain: Exact numbers with participant counts and clear framing build trust with employers and clients.

capstone.title: UX research pack and prototype
capstone.brief: Take one small, real task (for example booking an appointment, registering for an event or finding a certificate) through the full UX process and submit a research pack, a tested Figma prototype, a quality checklist, a findings report with before-and-after numbers, a case study with reflection on feedback, and a 90-day plan.
steps: Write a problem statement and 'How might we' question for one small task with users you can reach.
Interview at least 5 users with informed consent, group notes into themes, and build a one-page persona.
Draw a current-state journey map, run a quick card sort, and draw a user flow with error paths.
Sketch, then build mid-fidelity wireframes and a clickable prototype in Figma.
Run a heuristic review with severity ratings and the six-point accessibility checklist; fix severity 3 and 4 problems.
Test with 5 users (success, time, errors, SUS), fix the top problems, and test again with at least 3 more.
Apply simple visual design with components, then write your case study, reflection and 90-day plan.
evidence: Interview guide, photo of themed notes with counts, and persona
Journey map, card sort result and user flow
Figma prototype link and before-and-after screenshots
Heuristic review table and accessibility checklist
Usability test results for both rounds and a one-page findings report
Case study with a short reflection on what changed after feedback
90-day plan with weekly actions and targets
